$comment: Enumerated, dated exemptions from the exact-pinning rule enforced by
scripts/check-pins.mjs. This file is NOT a way to make pinning optional:
every entry must name a reason and a blocking decision, check-pins fails if
a waived specifier has become exact (a stale waiver must be deleted), and it
fails on any ranged specifier that is not listed here. The list may only

sdk-peer-contract.why: @underware/pistols-sdk is published (private: false, ~432 downloads/week) and declares this package in peerDependencies as 'catalog:'. pnpm rewrites 'catalog:' to the literal catalog version on publish, so pinning the catalog exactly would ship an exact peer requirement and break any consumer on a different patch (e.g. react 18.3.2 against a pinned react 18.3.1). A peer range is a deliberate contract, not laxity.
sdk-peer-contract.blocked_on: Decoupling the SDK's peerDependencies from the catalog so the internal resolution policy (exact) and the published consumer contract (ranged) are separate concerns. Needs a maintainer decision because it changes a published package's contract.
sdk-peer-contract.retires: When peerDependencies carry literal ranges instead of 'catalog:', at which point every entry above pins and this reason is deleted.

dead-entry.why: The 'dreams' workspace is disabled in pnpm-workspace.yaml, so this catalog entry resolves to nothing and cannot enter the dependency graph. There is no resolved version to pin it to.
dead-entry.blocked_on: Dependency-removal handling, deliberately deferred until the foundation is stable.
dead-entry.retires: When the entry is deleted, or the dreams workspace is re-enabled and the entry is pinned.
